commonProblem.graph: Unweighted complete undirected signed graph on n vertices; each pair is positive or negative.
commonProblem.objective: Minimize positive edges crossing clusters plus negative edges inside clusters.
commonProblem.mPositive: m⁺=|E⁺|, counting positive edges once, not total signed pairs and not negative edges.
commonProblem.parameterRange: 0≤m⁺≤n(n−1)/2; therefore n+m⁺ ranges from n to Θ(n²).
commonProblem.rangeMeaning: A family of resource upper bounds as density varies, not exact running time or a lower bound.

records.success: Expected approximation; not a high-probability factor-3 guarantee.
records.resourceProbability: The implementation bound holds for every random permutation.
records.inferenceScope: Adjacency-list resource bound only; expected factor 3 is the cited theorem.
records.inferenceExplanation: Use a uniformly random permutation and an assigned flag per vertex. An unassigned vertex becomes a pivot; scan its positive list and assign only unassigned neighbors to its cluster. Pivots form an independent set in G⁺, so each positive edge has at most one pivot endpoint and is queried at most once. At most n degree queries, m⁺ neighbor queries, O(n) permutation/flag/output work; total O(n+m⁺). The induced pivot distribution matches uniform selection from remaining vertices.
records.sourceLimit: The journal pseudocode loops over remaining vertices and does not itself state an O(n+m⁺) adjacency-list implementation theorem. Label the bound as implementation-derived.

records.theoremLocation: Full version Proposition B.1, printed p.38
records.guarantee: Every finite multiplicative approximation factor α≥1 requires Ω(n²) queries at success probability at least 99%.
records.timeConsequence: Ω(n²) time follows if one query costs O(1).
records.scopeWarning: Not a positive-list lower bound. Full signed-list degree is n−1; indexed neighbors reveal labels without filtering to positives.
records.proofIdea: A hidden positive pair among otherwise negative pairs yields zero-optimum instances, forcing a finite multiplicative approximation to distinguish the pair.

records.theoremLocation: Full version Proposition B.2, printed p.39
records.guarantee: Every finite multiplicative approximation factor α≥1 requires Ω(n²) queries at success probability at least 99%.
records.timeConsequence: Ω(n²) time follows if one query costs O(1).
records.scopeWarning: Not a positive-list lower bound. Access is filtered to G⁻. The proof discusses negative degree, pair, and neighbor queries.
records.proofIdea: The positive edges form a hidden perfect matching in zero-optimum instances; recovering an acceptable partition recovers that matching.
records.proofTranscriptionCaution: The full-version proof has an apparent degree-answer typo n−1 where its constructed negative graph has degree n−2. Cite the proposition and oracle scope rather than copying that proof line into the atlas.

exclusions: No nontrivial positive-list query lower theorem was verified in these two sources.
Do not reuse Assadi–Wang's cited MIS-computation lower bounds as lower bounds for arbitrary clustering algorithms.
ACN bad-triangle lower bounds on optimum and LP bounds are not query-complexity lower bounds.
Weighted correlation clustering, consensus clustering, additive-error matrix results, and streaming results are outside this pair review.
Do not substitute a numeric approximation factor for Assadi–Wang's unspecified constant.

implementationEvidence.graphFamily: All simple positive subgraphs on n=1,…,5; each defines a complete signed instance.
implementationEvidence.permutations: Every vertex permutation for every graph.
assertions: Positive-list implementation returns the same partition as recursive Pivot using the same ordering.
All vertices are assigned exactly once.
Total neighbor-list entries examined is at most m⁺.
implementationEvidence.limits: This is regression evidence for the stated implementation inference; the edge-count argument supplies its general proof. It is not a new approximation theorem.

figureProposal.mainAxis: Symbolic query-cost axis: n, n log n, n².
figureProposal.algorithms: Green markers/outline. AW point at n log n; Pivot density-dependent O(n+m⁺) upper-bound range with expected-factor label.
figureProposal.lowerBounds: Red diamonds at n² confined to alternative-oracle columns; labels retain any finite factor and ≥99% success.
figureProposal.setupColors: Distinct column tint/color with a separate setup legend; maintain green/red bound-type encoding.
figureProposal.time: Separate total-time chips, never silently mixed with query counts.
figureProposal.approximation: Use guarantee text, not a numeric approximation x-axis, because C=O(1) has no verified numeric value.
figureProposal.semanticZoom: Keep setup labels, named algorithms, asymptotic costs, and scoped red markers at atlas summary scale; hide theorem details/counts until focused inspection.
figureProposal.alternative: A shared total-time axis is also sound if query lower bounds are explicitly labeled as implying time lower bounds.
